title: openai-compat: reconcile Responses v12 seed & metadata passthrough with streaming tool handshake
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: OpenAI introduced a Responses v12 variant that exposes a client-facing deterministic seed and richer metadata attributes while slightly changing streaming chunk markers and tool-calling handshake timing. Customers using Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer observed two issues: (1) client-supplied seeds were not consistently propagated through retries, cache hits, and internal fallback to smaller model variants, and (2) structured attributes in the v12 responses (attributes, tags, provenance) were being dropped or transformed during proxying. Motivation: ensure parity with OpenAI Responses v12 semantics so downstream apps (tool routers, evals, rerankers) see deterministic outputs and the same metadata attributes across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. This PR implements a compatibility shim that (A) preserves the client seed (x-client-seed / request.seed) across the full request lifecycle including reconnects and retry resumes, (B) normalizes and forwards the v12 "attributes" map into Redwood's Response.Attributes field without flattening keys, (C) stabilizes streaming boundaries and reassembly logic to avoid duplicate tokens or missing tool-call markers when clients reconnect or when proxy re-streaming occurs, and (D) introduces a lightweight tool-handshake extension to the streaming protocol so tool availability signals arrive before tool calls in fragmented streams. Checklist: - [x] Propagate client seed into reroute/fallback paths and KV cache keys so cached responses respect determinism hints - [x] Add x-client-seed HTTP header and request.seed JSON support in OpenAI adapter - [x] Preserve attributes/tags/provenance as-is and add an attributes passthrough test-suite - [x] Rework streaming chunk reassembly to be idempotent for reconnects (sequence+fragment checks) - [x] Implement streaming preamble: TOOL_HANDSHAKE event emitted before first tool call fragment - [x] Add compatibility tests for Responses v12 examples and cross-variant fallbacks - [x] Update docs and API changelog notes for openai-compat v12 behavior and header guide Limitations / Notes: - This shim is conservative: when attribute keys conflict with Redwood internal keys we prefix incoming keys with "openai." to avoid accidental overwrites. - Determinism across quantized model fallbacks depends on identical sampling seeds; we surface warnings in the logs when fallback models are incompatible. - The handshake event is additive and ignored by older clients; the adapter will gracefully degrade if the client does not acknowledge the preamble.
commits_summary: 3 commits: initial adapter shim and header plumbing; streaming reassembly + handshake implementation; tests, docs, and perf tuning. Key commit messages: (1) openai-adapter: forward x-client-seed and seed JSON field to routing layer; (2) streaming: idempotent chunk-reassembler + TOOL_HANDSHAKE preamble; (3) compat-tests: responses-v12 attribute passthrough and reconnect scenarios + docs update.

// adapter.go: accept x-client-seed header and attach to RequestCtx
if hdr := req.Header.Get("X-Client-Seed"); hdr != "" { ctx = ctx.WithValue(ctx, metadata.ClientSeedKey, hdr) }

// streaming_reassembler.go: detect duplicate fragments by (seq,frag_id) and drop idempotent payload
if seenFragments.Has(key) { return nil }

// tool_handshake.proto: event definition for preamble
message ToolHandshake { repeated string tools = 1; map<string,string> meta = 2; }
review_discussion: Marcus Nguyen: Can we be explicit about how seeds are mixed with per-model RNG offsets? If two models sample differently this could give surprising determinism claims.

Asha Patel: Good point. Added a warning in fallback_manager when a fallback model has an incompatible sampler; we also preserve the original seed and annotate the response with response.meta.openai.fallback_sampler_mismatch=true.
Lena Ortiz: Streaming reassembly looks solid but we need a tiny optimization for the seenFragments cache to avoid unbounded growth under high-QPS. Suggest LRU + TTL.
Asha Patel: Implemented LRU+TTL and added a stress test; notes added in streaming_reassembler.go. Benchmark shows <3% p99 latency impact under 500 QPS.
Diego Ramos: Request-level e2e test failing intermittently in CI (race on attributes map). Please run with -race and ensure map copies are made.
Asha Patel: Fixed by deep-cloning incoming attribute maps before cross-thread usage; reran CI -race locally before pushing.

Marcus Nguyen: Approved after fixes.
Lena Ortiz: Approved.
Diego Ramos: Approved and left minor nit for docs grammar which was addressed.
release_notes: Compatibility: OpenAI Responses v12 - Redwood will now forward client-provided seeds via X-Client-Seed/request.seed and preserve v12 attributes/tags/provenance through the compatibility adapter. Streaming: improved reconnect resilience and TOOL_HANDSHAKE preamble to stabilize downstream toolcall ordering. Note: fallback to different sampler models may impact determinism; a warning flag is attached when sampler mismatch is detected.
